## Eager ops inside a captured stage: the user forcing and the chemistry segment {#sec-ch11-eagerops}

### Summary

Some ops of a stage cannot be captured, but the rest of the stage can. Such an op runs eagerly as a segment of its
own, between two captured segments, and is given the host step size. Two ops are of this kind when they are set.
A user TorchScript stage forcing is opaque to the executor. A registered chemistry step runs kintera's kinetics
in FP64, and kintera builds its tables on first use, which a recording refuses. On a bare block both run eagerly
inside the stage; the tendencies and the state cross the segment boundary in the block's fixed storage, which
the graphs on either side read and write. A block of a Mesh runs its chemistry the same way, as the eager segment
of its own last stage, before the Mesh's global phase (the axial closure).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Run an op that cannot be captured eagerly between captured segments, so the rest of the stage still
captures.

**Data.** The forcing reads the state and adds to the stage tendencies `du`, `ds`; the chemistry step reads and
writes `hydro_u` and `hydro_w`. Both read the host step.

**Placement.** The `forcing` op sits between `advance` and `combine`; the `chemistry` op between `saturation` and
`boundaries` (@sec-ch11-segments). A Mesh's chemistry runs after the last stage, before the final exchange.

**Activation.** `set_user_stage_forcings` on a block; `set_chemistry` on a block or a Mesh. Default: neither set,
and both ops capture as no-ops.

**Guarantee / limits.** A stage with such an op equals the eager stage bit for bit. Strict refuses it, as it has
an eager segment.

**Evidence.** `test_graph_user_forcing_python`, `test_graph_chemistry_slot_python`,
`test_graph_mesh_chemistry_python`, `test_sk4_chemistry_source_python` (@tbl-ch11-eagerops-tests).
:::

Local symbols of this section: none.

### Derivation

None: control flow. An eager op splits the captured run around it (@sec-ch11-segments), so a stage with a user
forcing has the segments [exchange], [advance], [forcing], [combine, saturation, chemistry, boundaries], and one
with a chemistry step on a bare block [exchange], [advance, forcing, combine, saturation], [chemistry],
[boundaries]. The captured segments read the device step (@sec-ch11-graphsafe), so their graphs serve every step;
the eager op reads the host step and keeps no graph.

### Numerical method

**When each op is eager.** `StageExecutor::user_forcing`
({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::user_forcing >}}) is true when the block holds a user stage
forcing; `StageExecutor::chemistry_slot` ({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::chemistry_slot >}})
is true when the block has a chemistry step and is not a block of a Mesh. `StageExecutor::build_schedule` then
marks the op not capturable, with the reason "a user TorchScript stage forcing is set" or "a chemistry step is
registered (eager FP64 kinetics, V3 C2)", and sets its `reads_host_dt`.

**A change after construction.** A forcing or chemistry step set after the block's first stage changes the
block's schedule signature (`StageExecutor::schedule_signature`); the next stage rebuilds the schedule and drops
the block's graphs, and the new segments are captured afresh.

**A Mesh's chemistry.** `MeshImpl::forward` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}) runs the blocks'
stages through the executor; a block with a chemistry step runs it there, on the pool, as the eager chemistry segment
of its last stage, exactly as a bare block does (`StageExecutor::chemistry_slot`,
{{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::chemistry_slot >}}). The global phase that follows holds the
axial closure only.

### Code

**How to use it.**

```python
block.set_user_stage_forcings(["forcing.pt"])   # a TorchScript module per forcing
block.set_chemistry(reactions)                  # kintera kinetics options
```

**What is refused, and why.** Nothing is refused without strict: the op runs eager and its reason is logged once.
With strict, the case stops before its first launch, naming the segment.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| a user forcing is set | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::user_forcing >}} | `StageExecutor::user_forcing` | `set_user_stage_forcings` |
| a chemistry step on a bare block | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::chemistry_slot >}} | `StageExecutor::chemistry_slot` | `set_chemistry` |
| the ops and their reasons | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::build_schedule >}} | `StageExecutor::build_schedule` | none |
| a Mesh's chemistry phase | {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}} | `MeshImpl::forward` | `set_chemistry` |

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_graph_user_forcing_python` | the forcing op runs eager between two graphs and the block equals an eager block in FP64 and FP32 with a changing step, also when the forcing is set after the block has captured; strict refuses the case | `torch.equal` (bitwise) | {{< code tests/test_graph_user_forcing.py >}} |
| `test_graph_chemistry_slot_python` | a 2-D moist column with a rain species and two kinetic reactions: the graph block captures and replays its compute segments, runs the chemistry segment eager, and equals eager in FP64 and FP32 after every step (state, failure counter, redo flag), with a step change, a rebind and an in-place edit; strict refuses the case; on CPU cuda-graph runs eager and equals eager | `torch.equal` (bitwise) | {{< code tests/test_graph_chemistry_slot.py >}} |
| `test_graph_mesh_chemistry_python` | a Mesh with a chemistry step captures its blocks' stages, runs each block's chemistry as the eager segment of its last stage, before the axial closure, and equals an eager Mesh | `torch.equal` (bitwise) | {{< code tests/test_graph_mesh_chemistry.py >}} |
| `test_sk4_chemistry_source_python` | on a reduced Jupiter cloud-resolving case, a block with a registered chemistry step equals a block stepped by hand with the same sequence (rates, Jacobian, one implicit step, species increment) after every step, in FP64 and FP32 | `torch.equal` (bitwise) | {{< code tests/test_sk4_chemistry_source.py >}} |

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A stage with an eager op launches its captured segments and the eager op separately, so it costs more launches
  than a stage captured whole.
- A Mesh runs its blocks' chemistry steps one after another, not on its worker pool, because kintera keeps
  process-global state in its evaporation kinetics.
:::
